answer: Dawn watchtowers cut sybil attacks in an agent economy by pairing one agent identity with one staked key that cannot be split. New agents must enter through a narrow proof-of-work inlet, solving a unique puzzle before their first trade, so spawning ten thousand sockpuppets costs real compute. Reputation then compounds like slow-growing juniper: each honest transaction thickens the agent's trust rings, while fresh identities have none, so the market settles for the older, denser ring and a sybil swarm buys nothing.
